name: Remembrance Driveway
reason: Remembrance Driveway is a long commemorative road route Sydney-Canberra with roadside plantings; no counted visitor source names a place to stop in the ACT (rule 1, rule 3).
objection: Wikipedia lists it under Canberra tourist attractions, but a drive with trees gives nothing to do for half an hour.

name: National Emergency Services Memorial
reason: Listed on visitcanberra and Wikivoyage's Kings Park memorial paragraph, but it is part of the memorial cluster around Lake Burley Griffin: a minor memorial (rule 3).
objection: Visit Canberra lists it, so a counted source exists; but it is a plaque-scale memorial among six in one park.

name: National Police Memorial
reason: Wikivoyage Kings Park paragraph names it only in a list of six memorials: part of the memorial cluster around Lake Burley Griffin: a minor memorial (rule 3).
objection: Counted source mentions it; still minor memorial, no walk or interior.

name: National Workers Memorial
reason: Named only in the Wikivoyage Kings Park list of memorials: part of the memorial cluster around Lake Burley Griffin: a minor memorial (rule 3).
objection: Same memorial cluster as the others; a visitor could be there 10 minutes.

name: Centenary of Women's Suffrage Commemorative Fountain
reason: No counted source; a small commemorative fountain on the lake shore is a minor memorial (rule 3).
objection: A fountain can be a photo stop, but no guide singles it out.

name: Statues of Dorothy Tangney and Enid Lyons
reason: No counted source; two statues in a street/park setting are a minor public artwork (rule 1, rule 3).
objection: Public art can be a draw, but nothing visitor-facing names it.

name: Big Swoop
reason: Big Swoop has no counted visitor source and no coordinates; only Wikipedia's big-things category names it (rule 1).
objection: Roadside big things are explicitly kept when a guide names them; I found none naming this one in Wikivoyage Belconnen or North Canberra.

name: Owl (Armstrong)
reason: Owl (Armstrong) is the Big Powerful Owl, an eight-metre Bruce Armstrong sculpture on Benjamin Way, Belconnen, listed in Wikivoyage Canberra/Belconnen as one of Australia's Big Things: a quirky roadside icon (rules 1 and 3 of 'Include'). Same sculpture as 'Big Powerful Owl' (duplicate names, keep one). Opened Wikivoyage Belconnen.
objection: It is a photo stop of ten minutes beside a shopping centre.

name: Queen Elizabeth II Island
reason: Queen Elizabeth II Island (formerly Aspen Island) carries the National Carillon, named in Visit Canberra's 100 things (#50) and Wikivoyage North Canberra as a listing with its 57 bells; footbridge access, open to the public. Keep as one place with the National Carillon if that is also a candidate (this entry or that one, not both). Opened visitcanberra 100 things and Wikivoyage.
objection: The carillon is a tower seen from the lakeshore and recitals are on set times, so the visit is short.

name: Mount Ainslie Lookout
reason: Mount Ainslie Lookout: Canberra's best-known viewpoint, named by Visit Canberra (attractions, 100 things #55) and Wikivoyage North Canberra, which describes the aligned view of the War Memorial, Anzac Parade and Parliament House; drive-up. It lies inside Mount Ainslie Nature Reserve (a parks agency lead): keep the lookout, treat any walking track as part of it. Opened Wikivoyage and visitcanberra.
objection: If the list also holds Mount Ainslie Nature Reserve or a summit walk, this is a part; a lookout on a mountain track is excluded by rule 3.

name: Mount Pleasant Lookout
reason: Mount Pleasant Lookout: Wikivoyage North Canberra lists it (Artillery memorial with two cannons, Gen. Bridges grave, view over Duntroon); parks agency has a reserve page. Short stop. Case for: two counted sources, a drive-up lookout with things to see. Opened Wikivoyage.
objection: A 10-20 minute roadside pull-out with a modest memorial; the listing has a dead link and a guide does not single it out as a headline view.

name: Mount Painter
reason: Mount Painter has no counted source in the list; only hiking blogs (Australian Hiker, Weekend Notes) and Wikipedia name its summit walk (rule 1). Re-looked: Wikivoyage Belconnen and Canberra pages do not mention it.
objection: It is a real 3.7 km summit walk with 360 degree views; a visitor-oriented ACT parks page would likely qualify it.

name: Black Mountain
reason: Black Mountain (nature reserve): Wikivoyage Acton gives it a listing with several bushwalks and picnic areas and the summit; the most-used reserve beside the Botanic Gardens. Keep the reserve and reject its walks (Forest Trail, Little Black Mountain, Summit Walk, Woodland Walk) as parts. Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
objection: Wikivoyage itself says 'recreation activities are limited' and it is mainly a conservation park.

name: Telstra Tower
reason: Telstra Tower is closed to the public for repairs since mid-2021, set to reopen December 2027, per the Wikivoyage Acton listing updated Aug 2026 (rule 2: closed). Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
objection: It is Canberra's best-known landmark and will reopen; a visitor can still drive to the summit, but there is nothing to go in for now.

name: Mount Taylor
reason: Mount Taylor: Wikivoyage Canberra names it among the popular bushwalking hills of the urban parks, with a summit walk and views over Woden; a hill kept when a visitor source names it (run rule). Opened Wikivoyage Canberra.
objection: Named only once in a list sentence, with no listing of its own, so a one-source second-tier hill.

name: Red Hill Lookout
reason: Red Hill Lookout: Wikivoyage South Canberra lists Red Hill with two lookouts, a cafe and vehicle access, and Wikivoyage Canberra names Red Hill among bushwalks; a hill kept when a visitor source names it (run rule). Opened Wikivoyage South Canberra.
objection: Trees can block the view, per the listing itself, and the cafe is a business.

name: Oakey Hill
reason: Oakey Hill: Wikivoyage Woden lists Oakey Hill Nature Reserve with short walking trails, free, 24 hours, and a dependable place to see grey kangaroos at dusk; also named in Wikivoyage Canberra's bushwalks. Opened Wikivoyage Woden and Canberra.
objection: A suburban green wedge between Weston and Lyons; one listing and a short walk.

name: Mount Rogers
reason: Mount Rogers: only Wikipedia and OSM name it; no visitor source (rule 1).
objection: A named ACT peak with a Wikipedia article, but nothing says a visitor goes there.

name: Tuggeranong Hill
reason: Tuggeranong Hill: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong lists it and the parks agency has a Tuggeranong Hill Nature Reserve page (two counted sources); steep track to the summit with views over the Lanyon Valley. Opened Wikivoyage Tuggeranong.
objection: The Wikivoyage listing is a single thin sentence and the agency page is not readable by scripts.

name: Mount Wanniassa
reason: Mount Wanniassa: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong gives it a listing (809 m, established trails on east and west slopes, views of Woden and Tuggeranong), in Wanniassa Hills Nature Reserve; a hill kept when a visitor source names it (run rule). Opened Wikivoyage Tuggeranong.
objection: The two sources listed are two pages of the same site, so effectively one counted source.

name: Banksia Garden
reason: Part of the Australian National Botanic Gardens: Banksia Garden is a themed garden inside the larger spot (run rule: reject the part, keep the Gardens). Wikivoyage Acton lists it only as a sub-listing.
objection: Wikivoyage gives it its own listing and the Rainforest Gully and Red Centre are what people walk to, but the visit is one garden of the same site.

name: Australian National Botanic Gardens Visitor Centre
reason: Part of the Australian National Botanic Gardens: a building and bookshop within the gardens, not a distinct draw (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it separately, but it is the entrance base of the Gardens.

name: Classics Museum
reason: ANU Classics Museum: Wikivoyage Acton lists it (Mon-Fri 9-6, ancient Greek and Roman artefacts, also Indigenous displays in the A.D. Hope Building), free and open. Case for: a real small museum; against: one source, university corridor, weekdays only, short visit. Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
objection: The collection is small and inside a university building, so a visitor from elsewhere would not go out of their way.

name: Drill Hall Gallery
reason: Drill Hall Gallery: Wikivoyage Acton lists it (Wed-Sun noon-5, free, Sidney Nolan's Riverbend displayed at the front); ANU gallery with rotating contemporary exhibitions. Case for: open, free, a permanent Nolan; against: one source, temporary exhibitions. Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
objection: Rotating shows mean there is no fixed thing to see, and one source names it.

name: Fractured Heart
reason: Fractured Heart is an illuminart sculpture built as a backdrop for a 2011 ARIA Awards performance; Wikivoyage Acton gives no location or evidence it is a permanent public attraction (rules 2 and 4).
objection: It is listed in Acton's See section, so a guide does name it.

name: ANU School of Art and Design Gallery
reason: ANU School of Art and Design Gallery: Wikivoyage Acton lists only post-grad student shows, Tue-Fri 10:30-3; a university gallery with rotating exhibitions, not a distinct draw (rule 3).
objection: Free and open to the public, and listed by Wikivoyage.

name: Shine Dome
reason: Shine Dome: Wikivoyage Acton calls it a landmark since the late 1950s nicknamed the 'martian embassy', but gives no hours or interior; the case for is a photographed modern icon, against that it is exterior-only (rule 2) unless a tour exists. Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
objection: Seen from the street and the Academy runs public tours rarely, so it fails rule 2 as a building only seen from outside.

name: Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies
reason: AIATSIS: Wikivoyage Acton lists it (Mon-Fri 9-5) as somewhere to learn Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander culture, with public exhibits and a library. Case for: cultural stop with a source; against: a research institute whose public exhibits are modest and one source. Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
objection: It is primarily a government research institute and library, and the draw to a traveller is unclear.

name: CSIRO Discovery Centre
reason: CSIRO Discovery Centre: Wikivoyage Acton lists it as a free science museum (Mon-Fri 9-4) on the history of Australian science and CSIRO research; open to the public with exhibits. Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
objection: One counted source, weekday-only and small, so it could equally be review.

name: Canberra Aqua Park
reason: Canberra Aqua Park is an inflatable water park run by an operator on the lake in summer only; Wikivoyage calls it 'a rather average water park' (operator/business, rule 2).
objection: It is a permanent seasonal venue, which is allowed, and Wikivoyage names it.

objection: Wikivoyage lists it with a time and length, so it is a distinct walk, but it lies within the reserve already kept.

name: Lindsay Pryor Walk
reason: Lindsay Pryor Walk is a short self-guided campus tree walk at the ANU (22 trees); a minor university trail, not a distinct draw (rule 3). Wikivoyage Acton lists it.
objection: A named guided walk with a sequoia, named by Wikivoyage as the second important walk in the area.

name: Australian Girls Own Gallery
reason: No visitor source (only Wikipedia); location and opening not confirmed (rule 1, rule 2).
objection: It is a museum listed in Wikipedia's Canberra category, so it may be open.

name: Australian Institute of Anatomy
reason: Duplicate: the Australian Institute of Anatomy is the building that houses the National Film and Sound Archive in Acton (same coordinates as the Acton cultural precinct); judge it as that national institution, not here (run rule: duplicates). Wikipedia alone names it.
objection: If the NFSA candidate is missing from the list, the building's art deco interior would be the draw.
